demos.title: Mean, median and mode from a data set
demos.blurb: Section A regularly asks for these three summaries. Change the scores and watch each one move.
demos.code:
# Mean, median and mode — the three summaries Section A asks for.
from collections import Counter

scores = [12, 15, 11, 18, 15, 20, 15, 9]
scores.sort()
n = len(scores)

mean = sum(scores) / n
median = scores[n // 2] if n % 2 else (scores[n // 2 - 1] + scores[n // 2]) / 2
mode = Counter(scores).most_common(1)[0]

print("sorted:", scores)
print(f"mean   = {mean:.2f}")
print(f"median = {median}")
print(f"mode   = {mode[0]} (appears {mode[1]} times)")

demos.title: Linear search vs binary search
demos.blurb: Same target, two algorithms. Count the comparisons — this is the evidence for O(n) versus O(log n).
demos.code:
# Linear search vs binary search: count the comparisons.
data = list(range(0, 100, 2))   # 50 even numbers, sorted
target = 74

linear_steps = 0
for value in data:
    linear_steps += 1
    if value == target:
        break

lo, hi, binary_steps = 0, len(data) - 1, 0
while lo <= hi:
    binary_steps += 1
    mid = (lo + hi) // 2
    if data[mid] == target:
        break
    if data[mid] < target:
        lo = mid + 1
    else:
        hi = mid - 1

print(f"{len(data)} items, target {target}")
print("linear comparisons:", linear_steps)
print("binary comparisons:", binary_steps)
print("binary search is O(log n); linear search is O(n)")

demos.title: Tests first, then the function
demos.blurb: Each assert is a test. Silence means they all passed — this is verification, as the marking scheme uses the word.
demos.code:
# Test-first development: write the tests, then the function.
def average(numbers):
    """Return the mean, or 0 for an empty list."""
    if not numbers:
        return 0
    return sum(numbers) / len(numbers)

# Each assert is a test. No output means every test passed.
assert average([10, 20, 30]) == 20
assert average([5]) == 5
assert average([]) == 0
assert round(average([2, 3]), 2) == 2.5

print("4 tests passed")

demos.title: Create and query a real SQLite database
demos.blurb: A real database, created in memory and queried with SQL. Edit the WHERE clause or add a row.
demos.code:
# SQLite runs inside the browser: real SQL, real rows.
import sqlite3

db = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
db.execute("CREATE TABLE student (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, mark INTEGER)")
db.executemany(
    "INSERT INTO student (name, mark) VALUES (?, ?)",
    [("Ada", 88), ("Grace", 91), ("Alan", 74)],
)

print("H1 students (mark >= 90):")
for row in db.execute(
    "SELECT name, mark FROM student WHERE mark >= 90 ORDER BY mark DESC"
):
    print(" ", row)

print("average mark:", db.execute("SELECT AVG(mark) FROM student").fetchone()[0])

demos.title: A Monte Carlo simulation of two dice
demos.blurb: More trials move the simulated mean towards the theoretical 7.00 — the point a modelling question wants you to make.
demos.code:
# A Monte Carlo simulation: roll two dice 10,000 times.
import random

trials = 10_000
total = 0
sevens = 0

for _ in range(trials):
    roll = random.randint(1, 6) + random.randint(1, 6)
    total += roll
    if roll == 7:
        sevens += 1

print("trials:", trials)
print(f"mean roll: {total / trials:.2f}  (true mean 7.00)")
print(f"sevens: {sevens} ({sevens / trials:.1%}, true 16.7%)")

demos.title: A nearest-centroid classifier from scratch
demos.blurb: Features, distance, label — a classifier with no libraries. Change the test points and watch the decision boundary.
demos.code:
# A nearest-centroid classifier, written from scratch.
# Features: [hours studied, hours slept]
h1_students = [[8, 7], [7, 8], [9, 6]]
pass_students = [[2, 5], [3, 4], [1, 6]]

def centroid(points):
    n = len(points)
    return [sum(p[i] for p in points) / n for i in range(len(points[0]))]

def distance(a, b):
    return sum((x - y) ** 2 for x, y in zip(a, b)) ** 0.5

c_h1 = centroid(h1_students)
c_pass = centroid(pass_students)

for student in [[8, 6], [3, 5], [6, 7]]:
    d1 = distance(student, c_h1)
    d2 = distance(student, c_pass)
    label = "H1" if d1 < d2 else "pass"
    print(f"{student}: H1 {d1:.2f} vs pass {d2:.2f} -> {label}")
